component_findings.async_structured: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: Asynchronous concurrency has first-class composition and structured lifetime/join/cancellation mechanisms or an equivalent disciplined model. Evidence basis: Go | Goroutines are lightweight (small growable initial stack), scheduled M:N onto OS threads by the runtime, enabling hundreds of thousands of concurrent goroutines cheaply. | Channels are a built-in typed primitive with direct syntax (chan, <-, select), implementing CSP-style message passing as a core language construct rather than a library addition. | select gives native multi-way non-blocking channel coordination; the standard-library context package provides pervasive cancellation/timeout propagation conventions. | Data-race detection is built into the toolchain (go run/test -race) via a first-party dynamic detector, giving strong diagnosability though it is dynamic rather than a static guarantee. | Go's type system does not statically prevent data races or enforce cross-goroutine ownership; shared mutable state via pointers/maps/slices can race without a compile error, unlike Rust's Send/Sync static concurrency safety. | sync package (Mutex, RWMutex, WaitGroup, atomic) supplements channels, giving a layered set of primitives (message passing + shared-memory sync) rather than forcing a single paradigm. | Adversarial corpus includes deep-recursion/large-file cases (e.g. ADV-21 variants at depth 1000/10000 and 200KB source) exercising goroutine stack growth and scheduler robustness under adversarial nesting. | No async/await function-coloring problem: goroutines make concur…

component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Go | Go's primary FFI mechanism is cgo, allowing calling C functions via `import "C"` pseudo-package with inline C in comments. | cgo introduces significant per-call overhead (goroutine-to-OS-thread transition, stack switching), roughly tens of ns and up, making tight-loop FFI expensive compared to zero-cost C interop in Rust, Zig, C/C++. | cgo breaks normal Go tooling: cross-compilation needs a C cross-compiler and CGO_ENABLED=1, static analysis coverage is incomplete for embedded C snippets. | No first-party lightweight non-cgo mechanism exists for calling arbitrary shared libraries; third-party pure-Go workarounds exist but signal an underlying language-level gap. | Passing Go pointers to C requires care due to the moving/relocating GC; cgo enforces pointer-passing rules at runtime, adding correctness burden absent in languages with non-relocating GC or manual memory management. | Struct/type marshaling between Go and C is manual (C.struct_X, C.CString/C.GoString, explicit frees) with no automatic ownership/lifetime tracking. | Go supports exporting Go functions to C via //export and building c-shared/c-archive artifacts, giving two-way interoperability -- a genuine positive. | No direct C++ ABI interop; C++ libraries require an extern C shim layer, an added indirection not required in Rust (bindgen), Zig, or C++ itself. | Reviewed programs/go/adversarial and programs/go/mic…
